_note:
ACT 4, BEAT 1: THE INFILTRATION. Meridian Foundation, the public atrium.

Canon: 'Lyra gets the player and Tarin into Meridian headquarters.' The hard part is that it must not read as a defection. She is seventeen, she still believes in her father, and at the end of Act 3 she watched a Commander read a drowned country and file a finding about the diameter. She is not changing sides here. She is somebody who has run out of ways to explain a thing away and has decided to look, and she is frightened of what looking is going to cost her.

So she does not sneak anybody in. She walks them through the front doors of a public building at eleven in the morning on visitor passes she signs in her own name, and that is worse than a night entry, because it means nothing here is hidden. The Foundation does not need to hide. The atrium this map draws is full of people queueing for flood relief and every one of those grants is real.

THE SURNAME. Canon says the player does not learn Lyra is Cassian's daughter 'at once'. Act 4 is where it lands, and it lands off a passing clerk rather than off a confession, because a secret that gets out by accident in a lobby costs her more than one she chose to tell. She does not soften it afterwards.

WHAT IT SETS. aur_hq_pass is this map's OWN flag and it was already built into it: aur_hq_gate is hidden by it, aur_hq_gate_open appears with it, and that one's line already says 'signed in by Miss Veyl herself'. This scene is the missing other end of that. aur_hq_gate is also removed live, because hiddenIfFlag is only evaluated when a map loads and the gate stands in the single gap in the counter at x=12.

lines: The ceiling is forty feet up and most of it is glass.
Every sound in the atrium arrives twice.
The relief queue goes out through the doors, and it is moving,
and the woman at the front of it is being given money.
I wanted this to be a horrible building.
I have wanted that since Stonewake and it is not going to happen, is it.
Somebody crosses the floor towards you at a completely normal speed,
which is how you can tell she has been waiting all morning.
Three days. I have read the same page of the same report three days running.
You are late and I am glad.
She has two visitor passes in her hand and she has been holding them long enough to bend them.
I did, and then I spent three days hoping you would not.
Both of those were true at once. It has been an unpleasant week.
Good. I would rather that than loyalty.
Loyalty is what got me twenty-two days of not asking anybody anything.
A clerk goes past at your shoulder with an armful of folders.
Morning, Miss Veyl.
...Veyl.
Cassian Veyl is my father.
I have known that since I was born and I should have said it on the ridge.
She does not look away and she does not soften any part of it.
Because the moment I say it, everything I tell you afterwards is a daughter talking.
I wanted one month of being believed on the evidence. I got it. It was worth having.
It changes everything, and you are being kind, which I am going to take.
Take it back later if you need to. I will still be standing here.

options.label: Then you can get us in.

lines: Yes. That is the other half of it and I have been dreading you working it out.
It is the only useful thing about me and I have never once used it.
Hear the shape of this before we go anywhere.
I have not decided that he is wrong.
I have asked four people in this building to tell me I am wrong.
All four of them changed the subject, and not one of them was clumsy about it.
That is not four people disagreeing with you.
That is four people who have all been told the same thing to say.
I know. I worked that out on Tuesday and I have not slept properly since.
Keep it in the bag and keep your hand out of the bag.
Nobody here can hear it. I would still rather nobody watched you holding it.
She has never once said out loud what it is.
I know what my father calls it and I know what it did to a room in a marsh.
Those are two pieces of knowing and I have stopped putting them together.
In this city? No.
There is nowhere in Aureline I would rather it was than in your bag. I hate that sentence.
She writes both passes out at the desk and signs them herself, in ink, with her own name.
The clerk countersigns without reading either of them.
Records is the stair in the far corner, past the counter. The hall is through the east door.
Nobody will stop you on either. Nobody has ever needed to.
{name}. Whatever is up there, we go up and we come back down.
Say it back to me.
...Fine. Do not say it back to me.
Just do the second half of it.
Records is at the back of the office floor and it is the dullest room in Caelora.
That is the whole trick of this place. I will be in there.
Look at the relief queue. Forty people, and every one of those grants is real money.
I have been trying all morning to make that mean he is a good man. It will not go.
It only means the building is real.
Right. Upstairs.

_note:
ACT 4, THE CLOSE. The player comes back down into the atrium with an empty key pocket and has to walk out through four hundred people being helped. That is the staging, and it is why the close is here rather than out in the square: the last thing Act 4 shows the player is the Foundation doing exactly the good it says it does, on the way out of the building that has just robbed them.

WEIGHTLESS ON THE MAP ON PURPOSE. Lyra catches them up in narration and leaves in narration, so this names no NPC, moves nothing and warps nowhere.

WHERE IT HANDS OFF. Lyra names Frostmere and the Observatory, which is where canon puts Elias' last message in Act 5, and she goes there herself, tonight, on a coach. NOTHING IN ACT 4 OPENS A ROAD NORTH and nothing should until Stage 5 builds one -- there must be no stub for a player to walk into -- so the thing the player is actually pointed at is Sorrell, in Hearthmere, which has existed since Act 1.

Listed after am_arrive because only the first 'enter' script that starts gets run: on this visit am_arrive declines on its onceFlag and this one takes its turn.

lines: The relief queue is shorter than it was this morning and it is still moving.
Nobody in this room knows. Nobody in it is ever going to know.
Somebody comes down the last of the west stair at a run,
which is the first thing she has done quickly all day.
I am going north. Tonight, on the mail coach, out of the east yard.
She has a coat over her arm and nothing else. She has not been home.
Frostmere. There is an observatory above the town and the Foundation pays for it,
and nobody has been up there in four years because there is nothing to see.
He kept a packet of your father's. Eleven years, unopened, and I know the drawer.
If it is anywhere it is up there, because it is the one place he never goes.
I have spent a year being his daughter about all of this.
I am going to go and be somebody else about it for a while and see how that fits.
Frostmere. The observatory above the town.
He kept a packet of your father's for eleven years and never opened it. I know the drawer.
I am not doing it for you, and I want that said where you can hear it.
I signed his name this afternoon. That is mine now, whatever else happens.
I would like to find out what I signed it for.
She does not say goodbye.
She goes out through the doors at a walk and the street closes over her in about nine steps.
Frostmere.
I have never been anywhere with snow in it.
That is the worst thing I have said all week and I know it was.
It was that or nothing, and I was not going to do nothing at you.
Sorrell first. She has written four times since the marsh and we have answered none of them.
She should hear this off us and not off a newspaper.
Out through the doors, and behind you the largest building in Caelora is going home.
The lights come off floor by floor, from the top.
Halfway across the square you put your hand in your bag without deciding to.
There is nothing in it to find.

_note:
STAGE 6, THE AFTERMATH, BEAT 2: LYRA REBUILDS MERIDIAN.

APPENDED to the Act 4 file rather than given one of its own, because the engine only loads data/events/<mapId>.json (Registry.loadScriptsFor) -- a scene that plays in this atrium has to live in this array or it is never fetched at all. Nothing above it is touched.

SAME ROOM AS THE FIRST BEAT OF ACT 4, DELIBERATELY. am_arrive opened on a relief queue going out through the doors with a woman at the front of it being given money, and the whole unease of Act 4 was that every true thing in this room stayed true. So the aftermath opens on the same shot. The queue is still moving. It was always real, and Lyra's decision is only worth anything because it was.

CANON: 'Lyra chooses to rebuild Meridian into something legitimate: conservation, ethical archaeology, disaster research. This is her arc landing, and it should be a decision rather than a reward.' So she has already decided before the player walks in, the player is not offered a vote on it, and the one thing she asks for is not approval. She asks somebody to be in the room. That is the difference between a decision and a reward, and the scene is built on it.

SHE IS NOT REPLACING HER FATHER AND THE SCRIPT SAYS SO. Three things kept, everything else burned, no survey floor, nothing under anything -- and an instruction to come back and burn it down if it ever grows a floor nobody talks about. Bond versus control, said by the daughter of the man who lost that argument.

GATE. act6_done, set by the climax; see the note on aftermath_quay in data/events/tideglass.json for the contract. Listed last in this array so that am_arrive and aur_act4_close both decline on their onceFlags before this one takes its turn -- only the first 'enter' script that starts is run.

WHAT IT HANDS ON. lyra_rebuilds, which the Foundation offices in Stonewake and Tideglass and the field voices in data/dialogue/common.json all read, and a pointer at the Summit registry on the other side of the city, which is where this stage ends.

lines: The atrium is louder than you have ever heard it and none of the noise is people talking.
It is paper.
Forty crates on a floor that has never had a crate on it,
and two clerks from the capital counting things into them out loud.
The relief queue goes out through the doors, and it is moving,
and the woman at the front of it is being given money.
It has not stopped once all week.
Nobody has asked it to.
Nine days.
Four hundred people upstairs found out what they had been part of by reading it in the Press.
Two resigned by letter. One came in anyway, sat down at her desk, cried for an hour,
and then did a full day of work. I have not stopped thinking about her.
The commission want the whole thing wound up. Papers, buildings, boats, the name struck off.
Six weeks and there would be nothing here at all.
She says it flatly, the way you say a thing you have already argued about with somebody and won.
That is the tidy answer. It costs eleven hundred people their wages
and it takes the pumps out of Marlbeck by the spring.
I have been the tidy answer's daughter my whole life.
I am not going to do the other half of him as well.
Three things kept and everything else burned.
I have written down which three and I have not shown it to anybody yet.
I know. That is not the question, and I would rather you did not hand me the easy one.
Everybody has, all week. It has not helped once.
Conservation. Kin, coast, fen, the lot, and no collecting.
Archaeology under the region's licence and not ours, with somebody from outside on every dig.
Disaster research. Published. Every figure, to anybody who asks, the week it is taken.
Storm cards stay free. They were always the only honest thing we printed.
No survey floor. No directorate that does not exist.
Nothing under anything, ever again.
There is one sheet in her hand with her own name already written at the bottom of it.
She has been holding it since before you came in.
I am not asking you to tell me it is a good idea.
I have had a week of that and it is worth nothing.
I am asking you to be standing there while I sign it.
So there is one person in the room who knows what it is instead of what it says.
You stay where you are.
She signs it against the end of the counter with a clerk's pen that is nearly dry,
and does not do it again more neatly.
The Meridian Foundation.
Eleven hundred people and three things.
If it ever gets big enough to have a floor nobody talks about, come back and burn it down.
I am saying that to you as an instruction and I would like it taken as one.
Behind her the relief queue moves up one.
Your friend has been in the Summit registry on the east side for two days,
pretending to read the standing list. Go and put him out of his misery.
